purpose: Standalone province-level reference table for rough savings estimates. For precise per-city/per-plan bill math see prices_json/ (built by rates_etl.py).

heating_oil_propane.name: NRCan Prices by City (Furnace Oil / Auto Propane)
heating_oil_propane.cadence: manual re-download (no stable API); furnace oil monthly, propane weekly
heating_oil_propane.method: simple mean across NRCan-surveyed cities per province, latest available reading per city (coverage varies by city); provinces with no surveyed cities use NRCan's own 'Canada' national-average column instead

city_province_caveats.Lloydminster: straddles the AB/SK border; assigned to AB here (unconfirmed against NRCan's own convention) — treat this city's contribution as low-confidence.
city_province_caveats.Grand Falls: assumed to be Grand Falls-Windsor, NL (NL's standard 5-city monitored set), not Grand Falls, NB.

heating_wood.name: Canadian Biomass Magazine — North America heating wood pellet market update, 2Q 2025
heating_wood.method: single flat $290/ton figure applied to every province — no province-level wood price source was found
assumptions: Price is assumed CAD, assumed short ton (2,000 lb / 907.185 kg) — the unit chart values in the source article render as an image, so these weren't independently confirmed from article text.
Energy content assumed at 16.5 million BTU/ton HHV, a standard figure for premium wood pellets (~8,250 BTU/lb) cited by pellet-industry fact sheets — this article doesn't state a heat content.
Converted: 16,500,000 BTU/ton x 0.00029307107 kWh/BTU = 4,835.7 kWh/ton delivered heat content; $290 / 4,835.7 kWh = $0.0600/kWh.
The source price may reflect wholesale/bulk market pricing rather than a residential retail rate; applying it to household heating cost is itself an approximation.

natural_gas_fallback.method: No residential gas utility in the canada-utility-rates tariff export for this province (may reflect no piped natural gas service, e.g. PE); filled with the unweighted mean of this table's other provinces' gas rates.

method.plan_selection: one plan per utility: time-of-use > tiered > flat/market > ultra-low-overnight
method.dedupe: latest effective_date per (utility, tariff name); ties broken by most-populated record
method.carbon: excluded (federal consumer fuel charge zero since 2025-04-01)
method.alberta: deregulated energy (RRO retailer) + wires (distribution utility) tariffs averaged within their own group, then summed as separate bills, plus screening estimates for upstream gaps (see per-province notes).

notes: Deregulated market: 3 energy retailer(s) averaged + 4 wires utility(ies) averaged, summed as separate bills.
Upstream distribution tariffs omit the transmission volumetric charge; a screening estimate of 0.017 $/kWh is added (same constant as prices_json/ab.json), confidence downgraded to low.
Federal carbon charge excluded (consumer fuel charge set to zero 2025-04-01).
Upstream tariffs omit the default gas commodity/supply charge; a screening estimate of 2.25 $/GJ is added (same constant as prices_json/ab.json), confidence downgraded.
No NRCan city-level data for this province; filled with NRCan's own 'Canada' national-average column from the same workbook.
